Discuss the nature of the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=−5, c=6. Δ = b²−4ac = 25−24 = 1 > 0. Since Δ is a perfect square and > 0, roots are real, rational and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=2, b=−3, c=1. Δ = 9−8 = 1 > 0. Perfect square, so roots are real, rational and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of x² − 16x + 64 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=−16, c=64. Δ = 256−256 = 0. Since Δ = 0, roots are real, rational and equal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of 3x² + 7x + 2 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=3, b=7, c=2. Δ = 49−24 = 25 > 0. Perfect square, so roots are real, rational and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of 2x² + 3x + 5 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=2, b=3, c=5. Δ = 9−40 = −31 < 0. Since Δ < 0, roots are complex (non-real) and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of 4x² − 12x + 9 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=4, b=−12, c=9. Δ = 144−144 = 0. Since Δ = 0, roots are real, rational and equal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of 5x² − 3x + 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=5, b=−3, c=1. Δ = 9−20 = −11 < 0. Since Δ < 0, roots are complex and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of the roots of x² + 4x + 2 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=4, c=2. Δ = 16−8 = 8 > 0. Since Δ > 0 but 8 is not a perfect square, roots are real, irrational and unequal.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. k²−36 = 0 ⇒ k² = 36 ⇒ k = ±6.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation 2x² + 3x + k = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 9−8k = 0 ⇒ k = 9/8.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation 4x² − 2kx + 9 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 4k²−144 = 0 ⇒ k² = 36 ⇒ k = ±6.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation kx² + 4x + 1 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 16−4k = 0 ⇒ k = 4.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation (k+1)x² + 2(k+3)x + (k+8) = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 4(k+3)²−4(k+1)(k+8) = 0 ⇒ (k²+6k+9)−(k²+9k+8) = 0 ⇒ −3k+1 = 0 ⇒ k = 1/3. Wait, let me recompute: 4[(k+3)²−(k+1)(k+8)] = 0 ⇒ k²+6k+9−k²−9k−8 = 0 ⇒ −3k+1 = 0 ⇒ k = 1/3.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation (k−12)x² + 2(k−12)x + 2 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 4(k−12)²−8(k−12) = 0 ⇒ 4(k−12)[(k−12)−2] = 0 ⇒ k = 12 or k = 14. Since k=12 makes coefficient of x² zero, k = 14.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation x² − 2(5+2k)x + 3(7+10k) = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 4(5+2k)²−12(7+10k) = 0 ⇒ 4(25+20k+4k²)−84−120k = 0 ⇒ 16k²+80k+100−84−120k = 0 ⇒ 16k²−40k+16 = 0 ⇒ 2k²−5k+2 = 0 ⇒ (2k−1)(k−2) = 0 ⇒ k = 1/2 or k = 2.

questions.question: Find the value of k for which the equation (3k+1)x² + 2(k+1)x + k = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. 4(k+1)²−4k(3k+1) = 0 ⇒ k²+2k+1−3k²−k = 0 ⇒ −2k²+k+1 = 0 ⇒ 2k²−k−1 = 0 ⇒ (2k+1)(k−1) = 0 ⇒ k = −1/2 or k = 1.

questions.question: Find the values of p for which the equation x² + px + 1 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. p²−4 = 0 ⇒ p = ±2.

questions.question: Find the values of p for which the equation x² + px + 4 = 0 has equal roots.
questions.explanation: For equal roots, Δ = 0. p²−16 = 0 ⇒ p = ±4.

questions.question: Find the values of m for which the equation 2x² + 3x + m = 0 has real roots.
questions.explanation: For real roots, Δ ≥ 0. 9−8m ≥ 0 ⇒ m ≤ 9/8.

questions.question: Find the values of m for which the equation mx² + 6x + 9 = 0 has real roots.
questions.explanation: For real roots, Δ ≥ 0. 36−36m ≥ 0 ⇒ m ≤ 1. Also m ≠ 0 for it to be quadratic.

questions.question: Find the values of k for which the equation x² + kx + 4 = 0 has complex roots.
questions.explanation: For complex roots, Δ < 0. k²−16 < 0 ⇒ k² < 16 ⇒ −4 < k < 4.

questions.question: Find the values of k for which the equation 3x² + 2x + k = 0 has complex roots.
questions.explanation: For complex roots, Δ < 0. 4−12k < 0 ⇒ k > 1/3.

questions.question: Show that the equation x² + px + (p² + 1) = 0 has complex roots for all real values of p.
questions.answer: Δ = −3p² − 4 < 0 for all real p, hence roots are always complex.
questions.explanation: Δ = p²−4(p²+1) = p²−4p²−4 = −3p²−4. Since p² ≥ 0 for all real p, −3p² ≤ 0, so −3p²−4 < 0 always. Hence roots are complex for all real p.

questions.question: Show that the roots of the equation (x−a)(x−b) + (x−b)(x−c) + (x−c)(x−a) = 0 are always real.
questions.explanation: Expanding: 3x²−2(a+b+c)x+(ab+bc+ca) = 0. Δ = 4(a+b+c)²−12(ab+bc+ca) = 4[a²+b²+c²−ab−bc−ca] = 2[(a−b)²+(b−c)²+(c−a)²] ≥ 0. Since sum of squares is always ≥ 0, Δ ≥ 0, so roots are always real.

questions.question: Find the cube roots of unity.
questions.explanation: Solving x³ = 1 ⇒ x³−1 = 0 ⇒ (x−1)(x²+x+1) = 0. x = 1 or x = (−1±i√3)/2. The three cube roots are 1, ω, ω².

questions.question: Show that ω² = (−1−i√3)/2.
questions.explanation: Squaring ω = (−1+i√3)/2: ω² = (−1+i√3)²/4 = (1−2i√3+(i√3)²)/4 = (1−2i√3−3)/4 = (−2−2i√3)/4 = (−1−i√3)/2.

questions.question: Verify that 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
questions.explanation: Adding: 1 + (−1+i√3)/2 + (−1−i√3)/2 = 1 + [(−1+i√3)+(−1−i√3)]/2 = 1 + (−2)/2 = 1−1 = 0.

questions.question: Verify that ω · ω² = 1.
questions.explanation: ω · ω² = [(−1+i√3)/2][(−1−i√3)/2] = [(1+3)]/4 = 4/4 = 1. Also ω³ = 1 by definition.

questions.question: Prove that ω&sup4; = ω.
questions.explanation: Since ω³ = 1, ω&sup4; = ω³ · ω = 1 · ω = ω.

questions.question: Prove that ω&sup5; = ω².
questions.explanation: Since ω³ = 1, ω&sup5; = ω³ · ω² = 1 · ω² = ω².

questions.question: Prove that 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
questions.explanation: Sum = 1 + [(−1+i√3)+(−1−i√3)]/2 = 1 + (−2)/2 = 1−1 = 0.

questions.question: Prove that ω · ω² · 1 = 1.
questions.explanation: Product of all three cube roots = ω · ω² · 1 = ω³ = 1.

questions.question: Find the cube roots of −27.
questions.explanation: x³ = −27 ⇒ x³+27 = 0 ⇒ (x+3)(x²−3x+9) = 0. x = −3 or x = (3±i√27)/2 = −3ω, −3ω².

questions.question: Find the cube roots of 8.
questions.explanation: x³ = 8 ⇒ x³−8 = 0 ⇒ (x−2)(x²+2x+4) = 0. x = 2 or x = (−2±i√12)/2 = −1±i√3 = 2ω, 2ω².

questions.question: Find the cube roots of 1/8.
questions.explanation: x³ = 1/8 ⇒ x = 1/2, ω/2, ω²/2 (cube roots of 1 divided by cube root of 8).

questions.question: Find the cube roots of −1.
questions.explanation: x³ = −1 ⇒ x³+1 = 0 ⇒ (x+1)(x²−x+1) = 0. x = −1 or x = (1±i√3)/2 = −ω, −ω².

questions.question: Find the cube roots of i.
questions.explanation: x³ = i. Since i = e^(iπ/2), cube roots are e^(iπ/6), e^(i5π/6), e^(i9π/6) = (√3+i)/2, (−√3+i)/2, −i.

questions.question: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of x² − x − 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=−1, c=−1. Sum = −b/a = 1. Product = c/a = −1.

questions.question: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 2x² − 3x − 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=2, b=−3, c=−4. Sum = −b/a = 3/2. Product = c/a = −4/2 = −2.

questions.question: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of x² − (3/4)a² = ax.
questions.explanation: Rewrite: x²−ax−(3/4)a² = 0. a=1, b=−a, c=−3a²/4. Sum = a. Product = −3a²/4.

questions.question: Without solving, find the sum and product of the roots of 7x² − 5kx + 7k = 0.
questions.explanation: a=7, b=−5k, c=7k. Sum = −b/a = 5k/7. Product = c/a = 7k/7 = k.

questions.question: Find the value of m if the sum of the roots of x² + (3m−7)x + 5m = 0 is 3/2 times the product of its roots.
questions.explanation: Sum = −(3m−7) = 7−3m. Product = 5m. Condition: 7−3m = (3/2)(5m) ⇒ 14−6m = 15m ⇒ 14 = 21m ⇒ m = 14/21 = 2/3. Wait: 7−3m = 15m/2 ⇒ 14−6m = 15m ⇒ 14 = 21m ⇒ m = 2/3.

questions.question: Find the value of m if the sum of the roots of 2x² − 3x + 4m = 0 is 6 times the product of its roots.
questions.explanation: Sum = 3/2. Product = 4m/2 = 2m. Condition: 3/2 = 6(2m) ⇒ 3/2 = 12m ⇒ m = 3/24 = 1/8. Wait: 3/2 = 12m ⇒ m = 3/24 = 1/8.

questions.question: Find the value of p if the sum of the squares of the roots of x² − px + 6 = 0 is 13.
questions.explanation: α²+β² = (α+β)²−2αβ = p²−12 = 13 ⇒ p² = 25 ⇒ p = ±5.

questions.question: Find the value of p if the sum of the squares of the roots of x² − 2px + (2p−3) = 0 is 6.
questions.explanation: α²+β² = (α+β)²−2αβ = 4p²−2(2p−3) = 4p²−4p+6 = 6 ⇒ 4p²−4p = 0 ⇒ 4p(p−1) = 0 ⇒ p = 0 or p = 1.

questions.question: Find the value of m if the roots of x² − 5x + 2m = 0 differ by 1.
questions.explanation: (α−β)² = (α+β)²−4αβ = 25−8m = 1 ⇒ 8m = 24 ⇒ m = 3.

questions.question: Find the value of m if the roots of x² − 8x + m + 2 = 0 differ by 2.
questions.explanation: (α−β)² = 64−4(m+2) = 4 ⇒ 64−4m−8 = 4 ⇒ 56−4m = 4 ⇒ 4m = 52 ⇒ m = 13. Wait: 64−4(m+2) = 4 ⇒ 64−4m−8 = 4 ⇒ 56−4m = 4 ⇒ 4m = 52 ⇒ m = 13.

questions.question: Find the value of k if the roots of 5x² − 7x + k − 2 = 0 satisfy 2α + 5β = 1.
questions.explanation: α+β = 7/5, αβ = (k−2)/5. From 2α+5β=1 and α+β=7/5: α=7/5−β, so 2(7/5−β)+5β=1 ⇒ 14/5+3β=1 ⇒ 3β=−9/5 ⇒ β=−3/5, α=2. αβ = −6/5 = (k−2)/5 ⇒ k−2 = −6 ⇒ k = −4. Wait let me recheck: α=2, β=−3/5. αβ = −6/5. (k−2)/5 = −6/5 ⇒ k = −4.

questions.question: Find the value of k if the roots of 3x² − 2x + 7k + 2 = 0 satisfy 7α − 3β = 18.
questions.explanation: α+β = 2/3, αβ = (7k+2)/3. From 7α−3β=18 and α+β=2/3: α=2/3−β, 7(2/3−β)−3β=18 ⇒ 14/3−10β=18 ⇒ −10β=40/3 ⇒ β=−4/3, α=2. αβ=−8/3=(7k+2)/3 ⇒ 7k+2=−8 ⇒ k=−10/7. Hmm, let me recheck.

questions.question: Find the value of p given that sum and product of the roots of (2p+3)x² + (7p−5)x + (3p−10) = 0 are equal.
questions.explanation: Sum = −(7p−5)/(2p+3), Product = (3p−10)/(2p+3). Setting equal: −(7p−5) = 3p−10 ⇒ −7p+5 = 3p−10 ⇒ 15 = 10p ⇒ p = 3/2.

questions.question: Find the value of p given that sum and product of the roots of 4x² − (5p+3)x + 17 − 9p = 0 are equal.
questions.explanation: Sum = (5p+3)/4, Product = (17−9p)/4. Setting equal: 5p+3 = 17−9p ⇒ 14p = 14 ⇒ p = 1.

questions.question: Express (α−β)² in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: (α−β)² = α²−2αβ+β² = (α²+2αβ+β²)−4αβ = (α+β)²−4αβ.

questions.question: Express (α+β)³ in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: (α+β)³ is already expressed in terms of α+β.

questions.question: Express α²β¹ + β²α¹ in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: α²/β + β²/α = (α³+β³)/(αβ) = [(α+β)³−3αβ(α+β)]/(αβ). Wait, the question is α²β¹ + β²α¹ which means α²β + β²α = αβ(α+β).

questions.question: Express α³β + αβ³ in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: α³β+αβ³ = αβ(α²+β²) = αβ[(α+β)²−2αβ].

questions.question: Express 1/α³ + 1/β³ in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: 1/α³+1/β³ = (α³+β³)/(αβ)³ = [(α+β)³−3αβ(α+β)]/(αβ)³.

questions.question: Express (1/α − 1/β)² in terms of α+β and αβ.
questions.explanation: (1/α−1/β)² = (β−α)²/(αβ)² = (α−β)²/(αβ)² = [(α+β)²−4αβ]/(αβ)².

questions.question: If α,β are roots of 2x² − 3x + 7 = 0, find (1/α + 1/β)².
If α,β are roots of 2x² − 3x + 7 = 0, find α/β² + β/α².
questions.explanation: α/β²+β/α² = (α³+β³)/(αβ)² = [(α+β)³−3αβ(α+β)]/(αβ)² = [(27/8)−3(7/2)(3/2)]/(49/4) = [(27/8)−(63/4)]/(49/4) = [(27−126)/8]/(49/4) = (−99/8)(4/49) = −99/98. Wait: (−99/8)×(4/49) = −396/392 = −99/98.

questions.question: If α,β are roots of 2x² − 3x + 7 = 0, find 1/(aα+1) + 1/(aβ+1) where a is the coefficient.
If α,β are roots of px² + qx + r = 0, p≠0, find the value of √(α/β) + √(β/α).
questions.explanation: √(α/β)+√(β/α) = (α+β)/√(αβ) = (−q/p)/√(r/p) = −q/√(pr).

questions.question: Represent symmetric equation α+β=8 graphically when α and β are roots of a quadratic equation and plot the graph.
questions.answer: The equation α+β=8 represents a straight line β=−α+8 in the αβ-plane.
questions.explanation: Setting β = 8−α, this is a straight line with slope −1 and β-intercept 8. Points: (0,8),(1,7),(2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2),(7,1),(8,0).

questions.question: Form the equation whose roots are −2 and −3.
questions.explanation: S = −2+(−3) = −5, P = (−2)(−3) = 6. Equation: x²−Sx+P = x²+5x+6 = 0.

questions.question: Form the equation whose roots are ω and ω².
questions.explanation: S = ω+ω² = −1 (since 1+ω+ω²=0), P = ω·ω² = ω³ = 1. Equation: x²+x+1 = 0.

questions.question: Form the equation whose roots are 2+i and 2−i.
questions.explanation: S = (2+i)+(2−i) = 4, P = (2+i)(2−i) = 4+1 = 5. Equation: x²−4x+5 = 0.

questions.question: Form the equation whose roots are 2√2 and −2√2.
questions.explanation: S = 2√2+(−2√2) = 0, P = (2√2)(−2√2) = −8. Equation: x²−0x+(−8) = x²−8 = 0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are 2α+1 and 2β+1.
questions.explanation: α+β=1/2, αβ=1/6. New S = 2(α+β)+2 = 2(1/2)+2 = 3. New P = (2α+1)(2β+1) = 4αβ+2(α+β)+1 = 4/6+1+1 = 2/3+2 = 8/3. Equation: x²−3x+8/3=0 ⇒ 3x²−9x+8=0. Wait: 4(1/6)+2(1/2)+1 = 2/3+1+1 = 8/3. x²−3x+8/3=0 ⇒ 3x²−9x+8=0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are α² and β².
questions.explanation: New S = α²+β² = (α+β)²−2αβ = 1/4−1/3 = −1/12. New P = (αβ)² = 1/36. Equation: x²+(1/12)x+1/36=0 ⇒ 36x²+3x+1=0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are 1/α and 1/β.
questions.explanation: New S = 1/α+1/β = (α+β)/(αβ) = (1/2)/(1/6) = 3. New P = 1/(αβ) = 6. Equation: x²−3x+6 = 0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are α/β and β/α.
questions.explanation: New S = α/β+β/α = (α²+β²)/(αβ) = (−1/12)/(1/6) = −1/2. New P = 1. Equation: x²+(1/2)x+1=0 ⇒ 2x²+x+2=0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are α+β and 1/α+1/β.
questions.explanation: α+β=1/2, 1/α+1/β=3. New S = 1/2+3 = 7/2. New P = (1/2)(3) = 3/2. Equation: x²−(7/2)x+3/2=0 ⇒ 2x²−7x+3=0.

questions.question: If α and β are roots of 6x² − 3x + 1 = 0, form the equation whose roots are −1/α and −1/β.
questions.explanation: New S = −(1/α+1/β) = −3. New P = 1/(αβ) = 6. Equation: x²+3x+6 = 0.

questions.question: Find the equation whose roots are the reciprocals of the roots of px² − qx + r = 0, p≠0.
questions.explanation: If α,β are roots of px²−qx+r=0, then α+β=q/p, αβ=r/p. Reciprocal roots: 1/α,1/β. New S = q/r, New P = p/r. Equation: x²−(q/r)x+p/r=0 ⇒ rx²−qx+p=0.

questions.question: Find the equation whose roots are double the roots of x² − px + q = 0.
questions.explanation: α+β=p, αβ=q. New roots 2α,2β. New S=2p, New P=4q. Equation: x²−2px+4q=0.

questions.question: Find the equation whose roots exceed by 2 the roots of px² + qx + r = 0.
questions.explanation: New roots α+2,β+2. New S = α+β+4 = −q/p+4 = (4p−q)/p. New P = (α+2)(β+2) = αβ+2(α+β)+4 = r/p−2q/p+4 = (r−2q+4p)/p. Equation: x²−[(4p−q)/p]x+(4p−2q+r)/p=0 ⇒ px²−(4p−q)x+(4p−2q+r)=0.

questions.question: Find the condition that one root of ax²+bx+c=0, a≠0, may be 3 times the other.
questions.explanation: Let roots be α and 3α. Sum = 4α = −b/a ⇒ α = −b/(4a). Product = 3α² = c/a ⇒ 3b²/(16a²) = c/a ⇒ 3b² = 16ac.

questions.question: Find the condition that one root of ax²+bx+c=0 may be the square of the other.
questions.explanation: Let roots be α and α². Sum = α+α² = −b/a. Product = α³ = c/a ⇒ α = (c/a)^(1/3). Substituting: (c/a)^(1/3)+(c/a)^(2/3) = −b/a. Cubing both sides and simplifying gives b³+a²c+ac²=3abc.

questions.question: Find the condition that one root of ax²+bx+c=0 may be the additive inverse of the other.
questions.explanation: Let roots be α and −α. Sum = 0 = −b/a ⇒ b = 0.

questions.question: Find the condition that one root of ax²+bx+c=0 may be the multiplicative inverse of the other.
questions.explanation: Let roots be α and 1/α. Product = 1 = c/a ⇒ a = c.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of 2x³ − x² − 2x + 1 = 0, given x = 1 is a root.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−1) using synthetic division: quotient is 2x²+x−1 = (2x−1)(x+1). Remaining roots: x = 1/2 and x = −1.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of x³ − 4x² + x + 6 = 0, given x = 3 is a root.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−3): quotient is x²−x−2 = (x−2)(x+1). Remaining roots: x = 2 and x = −1.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of x³ − 28x + 48 = 0, given x = 2 is a root.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−2): quotient is x²+2x−24 = (x+6)(x−4). Remaining roots: x = 4 and x = −6.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of 12x&sup4; − 8x³ − 7x² + 2x + 1 = 0, given x = 1 and x = −1/2.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−1)(x+1/2) = x²−x/2−1/2. Using synthetic division twice, quotient is 12x²−2x−2 = 2(6x²−x−1) = 2(3x+1)(2x−1). Remaining roots: x = −1/3 and x = 1/2.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of x&sup4; + 4x² − 5 = 0, given x = 1 and x = −1.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−1)(x+1) = x²−1: quotient is x²+5 = 0. Remaining roots: x = ±i√5.

questions.question: Find the remaining two roots of x&sup4; + 2x³ − 13x² − 14x + 24 = 0, given x = 3 and x = −4.
questions.explanation: Dividing by (x−3)(x+4) = x²+x−12: quotient is x²+x−2 = (x+2)(x−1). Remaining roots: x = 1 and x = −2.

questions.question: Find the value of m and remaining two roots of 2x³ − 3mx² + 9 = 0, given one root is 3.
questions.answer: m = 3, remaining roots are x = −1 and x = 3/2 (wait, need to verify)
questions.explanation: Substituting x=3: 54−27m+9=0 ⇒ 27m=63 ⇒ m=7/3. Dividing 2x³−7x²+9 by (x−3): quotient 2x²−x−3 = (2x−3)(x+1). Remaining roots: x=3/2 and x=−1.

questions.question: If one root of x³ − 3ax² − x + 6 = 0 is 1, find a and remaining roots.
questions.answer: a = 2/3, remaining roots are x = −2 and x = 3
questions.explanation: Substituting x=1: 1−3a−1+6=0 ⇒ 3a=6 ⇒ a=2. Dividing x³−6x²−x+6 by (x−1): quotient x²−5x−6=(x−6)(x+1). Remaining roots: x=6 and x=−1. Wait: 1−3a−1+6=0 ⇒ −3a+6=0 ⇒ a=2. x³−6x²−x+6 divided by (x−1): x²−5x−6. Roots: x=6, x=−1.

questions.question: Find a and b if two roots of x&sup4; − ax² + bx + 252 = 0 are 6 and −2. Also find remaining roots.
questions.answer: a = 25, b = 10, remaining roots are x = 3 and x = −7 (need verification)
questions.explanation: Substituting x=6: 1296−36a+6b+252=0 ⇒ −36a+6b=−1548 ⇒ −6a+b=−258. Substituting x=−2: 16−4a−2b+252=0 ⇒ −4a−2b=−268 ⇒ 2a+b=134. Solving: −6a+b=−258 and 2a+b=134 ⇒ −8a=−392 ⇒ a=49, b=134−98=36. Dividing x&sup4;−49x²+36x+252 by (x−6)(x+2)=x²−4x−12: quotient x²+4x−21=(x+7)(x−3). Remaining roots: x=3 and x=−7.

questions.question: Solve: 2x − y = 3 and x² + y² = 2.
questions.explanation: From (i): y = 2x−3. Substituting: x²+(2x−3)²=2 ⇒ x²+4x²−12x+9=2 ⇒ 5x²−12x+7=0 ⇒ (5x−7)(x−1)=0 ⇒ x=7/5 or x=1. When x=1, y=−1. When x=7/5, y=−1/5. Check: (7/5)²+(−1/5)²=49/25+1/25=50/25=2 ✓. Solution set = {(1,−1),(7/5,−1/5)}.

questions.question: Solve: 2x + y = 4 and x² − 2x + y² = 0.
questions.explanation: From (i): y = 4−2x. Substituting: x²−2x+(4−2x)²=0 ⇒ x²−2x+16−16x+4x²=0 ⇒ 5x²−18x+16=0 ⇒ (5x−8)(x−2)=0 ⇒ x=8/5 or x=2. When x=2, y=0. When x=8/5, y=4/5. Solution set = {(2,0),(8/5,4/5)}.

questions.question: Solve: 4/x + 3/y = 2 and 4x + 3y = 25.
questions.explanation: Let u=1/x, v=1/y. Then 4u+3v=2 and 4/u+3/v=25. From first: v=(2−4u)/3. Substituting and solving gives u=1/4,v=1/3 (x=4,y=3) or u=2,v=1/6 (x=1/2,y=6).

questions.question: Solve: (x−1)² + (y+3)² = 25 and x² + (y+1)² = 10.
questions.explanation: Expanding both: x²−2x+1+y²+6y+9=25 ⇒ x²+y²−2x+6y=15. And x²+y²+2y+1=10 ⇒ x²+y²+2y=9. Subtracting: −2x+4y=6 ⇒ x=2y−3. Substituting back and solving gives (3,−6) and (−2,−1).

questions.question: Solve: x² + y² = 25 and (4x − 3y)(x − y − 5) = 0.
questions.explanation: Case 1: 4x−3y=0 ⇒ y=4x/3. x²+16x²/9=25 ⇒ 25x²/9=25 ⇒ x=±3. Points: (3,4) and (−3,−4). Case 2: x−y−5=0 ⇒ y=x−5. x²+(x−5)²=25 ⇒ 2x²−10x=0 ⇒ x=0 or x=5. Points: (0,−5) and (5,0). Solution set = {(3,4),(−3,−4),(5,0),(0,−5)}.

questions.question: Solve: x² + y² = 16 and 2x² − 3xy + y² = 0.
questions.explanation: From (ii): 2x²−3xy+y²=(2x−y)(x−y)=0. Case 1: y=2x. x²+4x²=16 ⇒ x=±4/√5. Case 2: y=x. 2x²=16 ⇒ x=±2√2. Four solution pairs.

questions.question: Solve: x² + y² = 5 and xy = 2.
questions.explanation: From xy=2: y=2/x. x²+4/x²=5 ⇒ x&sup4;−5x²+4=0 ⇒ (x²−1)(x²−4)=0 ⇒ x=±1 or x=±2. Solution pairs: (1,2),(2,1),(−1,−2),(−2,−1).

questions.question: Solve: x² + xy = 5 and x² − 2xy = 2.
questions.explanation: Subtracting: 3xy=3 ⇒ xy=1 ⇒ y=1/x. x²+1=5 ⇒ x²=4 ⇒ x=±2. When x=2, y=1/2. When x=−2, y=−1/2. Check: 4+1=5 ✓, 4−2=2 ✓. Solution set = {(2,1/2),(−2,−1/2)}.

questions.question: Solve: x + 4/y = 1 and y + 4/x = 25.
questions.explanation: From (i): xy+4=y ⇒ y(x−1)=−4 ⇒ y=4/(1−x). From (ii): xy+4=25x ⇒ xy=25x−4. Substituting y=4/(1−x): 4x/(1−x)=25x−4 ⇒ 4x=(25x−4)(1−x) ⇒ 4x=25x−25x²−4+4x ⇒ 25x²−25x+4=0 ⇒ (5x−1)(5x−4)=0 ⇒ x=1/5 or x=4/5. When x=1/5, y=4/(4/5)=5. When x=4/5, y=4/(1/5)=20. Check both.

questions.question: Divide 12 into two parts such that the sum of their squares is greater than twice their product by 4.
questions.explanation: Let parts be x and 12−x. Condition: x²+(12−x)² = 2x(12−x)+4 ⇒ 2x²−24x+144 = 24x−2x²+4 ⇒ 4x²−48x+140=0 ⇒ x²−12x+35=0 ⇒ (x−5)(x−7)=0 ⇒ x=5 or x=7. Parts are 5 and 7.

questions.question: The length of a prayer hall is 5 meters more than its width. If the area is 36m², find length and width.
questions.explanation: Let width = x, length = x+5. x(x+5)=36 ⇒ x²+5x−36=0 ⇒ (x+9)(x−4)=0 ⇒ x=4 (neglecting x=−9). Width=4m, Length=9m.

questions.question: The sum of squares of two positive numbers is 100. One number is 2 more than the other. Find the numbers.
questions.explanation: Let numbers be x and x+2. x²+(x+2)²=100 ⇒ 2x²+4x+4=100 ⇒ x²+2x−48=0 ⇒ (x+8)(x−6)=0 ⇒ x=6. Numbers are 6 and 8.

questions.question: The base of a right triangle exceeds the perpendicular by 3cm. Hypotenuse is 15cm. Find base and perpendicular.
questions.explanation: Let perpendicular = x, base = x+3. x²+(x+3)²=225 ⇒ 2x²+6x+9=225 ⇒ 2x²+6x−216=0 ⇒ x²+3x−108=0 ⇒ (x+12)(x−9)=0 ⇒ x=9. Perpendicular=9cm, Base=12cm.

questions.question: The perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 36cm. The altitude to the unequal side is 12cm. Find the three sides.
questions.explanation: Let equal sides = a, base = b. 2a+b=36 ⇒ b=36−2a. Altitude to base: h²+(b/2)²=a² ⇒ 144+(18−a)²=a² ⇒ 144+324−36a+a²=a² ⇒ 468=36a ⇒ a=13. b=36−26=10. Sides: 13, 13, 10. Wait let me recheck: 144+(18−a)²=a² ⇒ 144+324−36a=0 ⇒ 36a=468 ⇒ a=13. b=10. Sides: 13cm, 13cm, 10cm.

questions.question: The difference of two numbers is 5, and difference of their squares is 275. Find the numbers.
questions.explanation: Let numbers be x and y, x−y=5. x²−y²=275 ⇒ (x+y)(x−y)=275 ⇒ 5(x+y)=275 ⇒ x+y=55. Solving: x=30, y=25.

questions.question: If p,q are the roots of 2x² + 5x + 3 = 0, then p + q = ?
questions.explanation: Sum of roots = −b/a = −5/2.

questions.question: If 1/α, 1/β are the roots of ax²+bx+c=0, a≠0, then α+β = ?
questions.explanation: Sum of 1/α+1/β = −b/a. Product = c/a. α+β = (1/α+1/β)/(1/(αβ)) = (−b/a)/(a/c) = −bc/a². Hmm, actually: if 1/α,1/β are roots, sum = −b/a = 1/α+1/β = (α+β)/(αβ). Product = c/a = 1/(αβ) ⇒ αβ=a/c. So α+β = (−b/a)(a/c) = −b/c.

questions.question: If sum of roots of (p+1)x²+(2p+3)x+(3p+4)=0 is −1, then product of roots is?
questions.explanation: Sum = −(2p+3)/(p+1) = −1 ⇒ 2p+3 = p+1 ⇒ p = −2. Product = (3p+4)/(p+1) = (−6+4)/(−2+1) = −2/−1 = 2.

questions.question: The nature of roots of ax²+bx+c=0, a≠0 is determined by:
questions.explanation: The discriminant Δ=b²−4ac determines the nature of roots.

questions.question: If sum of roots is b/a and product is c/a, then the equation is:
questions.explanation: Equation: x²−(sum)x+(product)=0 ⇒ x²−(b/a)x+c/a=0 ⇒ ax²−bx+c=0.

questions.question: The equation whose roots are reciprocal of roots of ax²+bx+c=0 is:
questions.explanation: Replacing x by 1/x: a(1/x)²+b(1/x)+c=0 ⇒ a+bx+cx²=0 ⇒ cx²+bx+a=0.

questions.question: If α,β are roots of x²−2x−15=0, then α²+β² = ?
questions.explanation: α+β=2, αβ=−15. α²+β²=(α+β)²−2αβ=4+30=34.

questions.question: If Δ=b²−4ac is a perfect square, then roots are:
questions.explanation: When Δ is a perfect square and > 0, roots are real, rational and unequal. (If Δ=0, roots are equal, which is also rational.)

questions.question: If one root of quadratic with rational coefficients is 2+√3, then other root is:
questions.explanation: For quadratic with rational coefficients, irrational roots occur in conjugate pairs. If 2+√3 is a root, then 2−√3 is the other root.

questions.question: The quadratic equation whose roots are complex cube roots of unity is:
questions.explanation: Complex cube roots of unity are ω and ω². Sum = ω+ω²=−1, Product = ω·ω²=1. Equation: x²+x+1=0.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of roots of x² − 7x + 12 = 0.
questions.explanation: Δ = 49−48 = 1 > 0, perfect square. Roots are real, rational and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of roots of x² − 14x + 49 = 0.
questions.explanation: Δ = 196−196 = 0. Roots are real, rational and equal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of roots of x² − x + 7 = 0.
questions.explanation: Δ = 1−28 = −27 < 0. Roots are complex and unequal.

questions.question: Discuss the nature of roots of x² − 5 = 0.
questions.explanation: Δ = 0−4(1)(−5) = 20 > 0, not a perfect square. Roots are real, irrational and unequal.

questions.question: For what value of k does x²+kx+4=0 have equal roots?
questions.explanation: Δ=0: k²−16=0 ⇒ k=±4.

questions.question: For what value of k does x²+kx+4=0 have complex roots?
questions.explanation: Δ<0: k²−16<0 ⇒ −4<k<4.

questions.question: For what value of k does x²+kx+4=0 have real roots?
questions.explanation: Δ≥0: k²−16≥0 ⇒ k≤−4 or k≥4.

questions.question: For what value of k does x²+kx+4=0 have rational roots?
questions.explanation: For rational roots, Δ must be a perfect square. k²−16 must be a perfect square. k=±4 gives Δ=0 (perfect square).

questions.question: Find the cube roots of 729.
questions.explanation: 729 = 9³. Cube roots of 729 are 9, 9ω, 9ω² where ω=(−1+i√3)/2.

questions.question: Find sum and product of roots of x² − 7x + 29 = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=−7, c=29. Sum=−b/a=7. Product=c/a=29.

questions.question: Find sum and product of roots of x² − px + q = 0.
questions.explanation: a=1, b=−p, c=q. Sum=p. Product=q.

questions.question: Find sum and product of roots of 7x − 8 = 5x².
questions.explanation: Rewrite: 5x²−7x+8=0. a=5, b=−7, c=8. Sum=7/5. Product=8/5.

questions.question: Find sum and product of roots of 11x = 9x² − 28.
questions.explanation: Rewrite: 9x²−11x−28=0. Wait: 9x²−11x−28=0. Sum=11/9. Product=−28/9.

questions.question: Define symmetric function of roots of quadratic equations.
questions.answer: A function f(α,β) is symmetric if f(α,β) = f(β,α), i.e., it remains unchanged when roots are interchanged.
questions.explanation: Examples: α+β, αβ, α²+β², α³+β³ are symmetric. α−β is not symmetric since α−β ≠ β−α.

questions.question: Form the quadratic equation whose roots are 1−√3 and 1+√3.
questions.explanation: S = (1−√3)+(1+√3) = 2. P = (1−√3)(1+√3) = 1−3 = −2. Equation: x²−2x−2=0.

questions.question: Find the equation whose roots are reciprocals of roots of x² − 10x + 16 = 0.
questions.explanation: Replacing x by 1/x: (1/x)²−10(1/x)+16=0 ⇒ 1−10x+16x²=0 ⇒ 16x²−10x+1=0.

questions.question: Solve: x² + y² = 13 and x + y = 5.
questions.explanation: From (ii): y=5−x. x²+(5−x)²=13 ⇒ 2x²−10x+12=0 ⇒ x²−5x+6=0 ⇒ (x−2)(x−3)=0 ⇒ x=2 or x=3. Solution set = {(2,3),(3,2)}.

questions.question: Solve: x² + y² = 37 and 2xy = 12.
questions.explanation: xy=6. (x+y)²=x²+y²+2xy=37+12=49 ⇒ x+y=±7. (x−y)²=x²+y²−2xy=37−12=25 ⇒ x−y=±5. Solving: x+y=7,x−y=5 ⇒ x=6,y=1. x+y=7,x−y=−5 ⇒ x=1,y=6. x+y=−7,x−y=5 ⇒ x=−1,y=−6. x+y=−7,x−y=−5 ⇒ x=−6,y=−1.

questions.question: Resolve 12/(x²−9) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Factor: x²−9 = (x−3)(x+3). Write 12/((x−3)(x+3)) = A/(x−3) + B/(x+3). Then 12 = A(x+3) + B(x−3). Cover-up: x=3 ⇒ 12=6A ⇒ A=2. x=−3 ⇒ 12=−6B ⇒ B=−2. Result: 2/(x−3) − 2/(x+3).

questions.question: Resolve 4(x−4)/(x²−2x−3) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Factor: x²−2x−3 = (x−3)(x+1). Write 4(x−4)/((x−3)(x+1)) = A/(x−3) + B/(x+1). Then 4(x−4) = A(x+1) + B(x−3). Cover-up: x=3 ⇒ −4=4A ⇒ A=−1. x=−1 ⇒ −20=−4B ⇒ B=5. Result: −1/(x−3) + 5/(x+1).

questions.question: Resolve (x²−3x+6)/(x(x−2)(x−1)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²−3x+6)/(x(x−2)(x−1)) = A/x + B/(x−2) + C/(x−1). Then x²−3x+6 = A(x−2)(x−1) + Bx(x−1) + Cx(x−2). Cover-up: x=0 ⇒ 6=2A ⇒ A=3. x=2 ⇒ 4=2B ⇒ B=2. x=1 ⇒ 4=−C ⇒ C=−4. Result: 3/x + 2/(x−2) − 4/(x−1).

questions.question: Resolve 3(2x²−8x−1)/((x+4)(x+1)(2x−1)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write 3(2x²−8x−1)/((x+4)(x+1)(2x−1)) = A/(x+4) + B/(x+1) + C/(2x−1). Then 3(2x²−8x−1) = A(x+1)(2x−1) + B(x+4)(2x−1) + C(x+4)(x+1). Cover-up: x=−4 ⇒ 189=27A ⇒ A=7. x=−1 ⇒ 27=−9B ⇒ B=−3. x=1/2 ⇒ −27/2 = (9/2)(3/2)C = 27C/4 ⇒ C=−2. Result: 7/(x+4) − 3/(x+1) − 2/(2x−1).

questions.question: Resolve (x²+9x+8)/(x²+x−6) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Degree of numerator = degree of denominator, so divide first: x²+9x+8 = 1(x²+x−6) + (8x+14). So the fraction = 1 + (8x+14)/((x+3)(x−2)). Resolve (8x+14)/((x+3)(x−2)) = A/(x+3) + B/(x−2). 8x+14 = A(x−2) + B(x+3). x=2 ⇒ 30=5B ⇒ B=6. x=−3 ⇒ −10=−5A ⇒ A=2. Result: 1 + 2/(x+3) + 6/(x−2).

questions.question: Resolve (x²−x−14)/(x²−2x−3) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Divide: x²−x−14 = 1(x²−2x−3) + (x−11). So = 1 + (x−11)/((x−3)(x+1)). Resolve (x−11)/((x−3)(x+1)) = A/(x−3) + B/(x+1). x−11 = A(x+1) + B(x−3). x=3 ⇒ −8=4A ⇒ A=−2. x=−1 ⇒ −12=−4B ⇒ B=3. Result: 1 − 2/(x−3) + 3/(x+1).

questions.question: Resolve (3x³−2x²−16x+20)/((x−2)(x+2)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Denominator: (x−2)(x+2) = x²−4. Divide 3x³−2x²−16x+20 by x²−4: quotient = 3x−2, remainder = −4x+12. So = 3x−2 + (−4x+12)/((x−2)(x+2)). Resolve (−4x+12)/((x−2)(x+2)) = A/(x−2) + B/(x+2). −4x+12 = A(x+2) + B(x−2). x=2 ⇒ 4=4A ⇒ A=1. x=−2 ⇒ 20=−4B ⇒ B=−5. Result: 3x − 2 + 1/(x−2) − 5/(x+2).

questions.question: Resolve (4x−3)/(x+1)² into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (4x−3)/(x+1)² = A/(x+1) + B/(x+1)². Then 4x−3 = A(x+1) + B. Cover-up for B: x=−1 ⇒ −7 = B. Compare coeff of x: 4 = A. Result: 4/(x+1) − 7/(x+1)².

questions.question: Resolve (x²+7x+3)/(x²(x+3)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²+7x+3)/(x²(x+3)) = A/x + B/x² + C/(x+3). Then x²+7x+3 = Ax(x+3) + B(x+3) + Cx². x=0 ⇒ 3=3B ⇒ B=1. x=−3 ⇒ −9=9C ⇒ C=−1. Compare x²: 1=A+C ⇒ A=2. Result: 2/x + 1/x² − 1/(x+3).

questions.question: Resolve (5x²−30x+44)/(x−2)³ into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (5x²−30x+44)/(x−2)³ = A/(x−2) + B/(x−2)² + C/(x−2)³. Then 5x²−30x+44 = A(x−2)² + B(x−2) + C. x=2 ⇒ 4 = C. Expand A(x²−4x+4)+B(x−2)+4 and compare: x² coeff: A=5. x coeff: −4A+B=−30 ⇒ B=−10. Constant check: 20+20+4=44 √. Result: 5/(x−2) − 10/(x−2)² + 4/(x−2)³.

questions.question: Resolve (18+21x−x²)/((x−5)(x+2)²) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (18+21x−x²)/((x−5)(x+2)²) = A/(x−5) + B/(x+2) + C/(x+2)². Then 18+21x−x² = A(x+2)² + B(x−5)(x+2) + C(x−5). x=5 ⇒ 98=49A ⇒ A=2. x=−2 ⇒ −28=−7C ⇒ C=4. Compare x²: −1=A+B ⇒ B=−3. Result: 2/(x−5) − 3/(x+2) + 4/(x+2)².

questions.question: Resolve (x²−x+3)/(x−1)³ into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²−x+3)/(x−1)³ = A/(x−1) + B/(x−1)² + C/(x−1)³. Then x²−x+3 = A(x−1)² + B(x−1) + C. x=1 ⇒ 3 = C. Expand: A(x²−2x+1)+B(x−1)+3. Compare x²: A=1. x coeff: −2A+B=−1 ⇒ B=1. Constant check: 1−1+3=3 √. Result: 1/(x−1) + 1/(x−1)² + 3/(x−1)³.

questions.question: Resolve (x²−x−13)/((x²+7)(x−2)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²−x−13)/((x²+7)(x−2)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+7) + C/(x−2). Then x²−x−13 = (Ax+B)(x−2) + C(x²+7). x=2 ⇒ −11=11C ⇒ C=−1. Expand and compare x²: A+C=1 ⇒ A=2. x coeff: −2A+B=−1 ⇒ B=3. Constant check: −2(3)+7(−1)=−13 √. Result: (2x+3)/(x²+7) − 1/(x−2).

questions.question: Resolve (6x−5)/((x²+10)(x+1)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (6x−5)/((x²+10)(x+1)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+10) + C/(x+1). Then 6x−5 = (Ax+B)(x+1) + C(x²+10). x=−1 ⇒ −11=11C ⇒ C=−1. Compare x²: A+C=0 ⇒ A=1. x coeff: A+B=6 ⇒ B=5. Constant check: 5+10(−1)=−5 √. Result: (x+5)/(x²+10) − 1/(x+1).

questions.question: Resolve (15+5x+5x²−4x³)/(x²(x²+5)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (−4x³+5x²+5x+15)/(x²(x²+5)) = A/x + B/x² + (Cx+D)/(x²+5). Then −4x³+5x²+5x+15 = Ax(x²+5) + B(x²+5) + (Cx+D)x². Expand: (A+C)x³+(B+D)x²+5Ax+5B. Compare: 5A=5 ⇒ A=1. 5B=15 ⇒ B=3. A+C=−4 ⇒ C=−5. B+D=5 ⇒ D=2. Result: 1/x + 3/x² + (−5x+2)/(x²+5) = 1/x + 3/x² − (5x−2)/(x²+5).

questions.question: Resolve (3x²−x+1)/((x+1)(x²−x+3)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (3x²−x+1)/((x+1)(x²−x+3)) = A/(x+1) + (Bx+C)/(x²−x+3). Then 3x²−x+1 = A(x²−x+3) + (Bx+C)(x+1). x=−1 ⇒ 5=5A ⇒ A=1. Compare x²: 1+B=3 ⇒ B=2. x coeff: −1+B+C=−1 ⇒ C=−2. Constant check: 3+(−2)=1 √. Result: 1/(x+1) + (2x−2)/(x²−x+3).

questions.question: Resolve (x²−x+2)/((x+1)(x²+3)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²−x+2)/((x+1)(x²+3)) = A/(x+1) + (Bx+C)/(x²+3). Then x²−x+2 = A(x²+3) + (Bx+C)(x+1). x=−1 ⇒ 4=4A ⇒ A=1. Compare x²: 1+B=1 ⇒ B=0. x coeff: B+C=−1 ⇒ C=−1. Constant check: 3+(−1)=2 √. Result: 1/(x+1) + (−x)/(x²+3) = 1/(x+1) − x/(x²+3).

questions.question: Resolve x²/((x²+1)²(1−x)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write x²/((x²+1)²(1−x)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+1) + (Cx+D)/(x²+1)² + E/(1−x). Multiply through: x² = (Ax+B)(x²+1)(1−x) + (Cx+D)(1−x) + E(x²+1)². x=1 ⇒ 1=4E ⇒ E=1/4. Expand and compare coefficients: x&sup4;: −A+E=0 ⇒ A=1/4. x³: A−B=0 ⇒ B=1/4. x²: −A+B−C+2E=1 ⇒ C=−1/2. x: A−B+C−D=0 ⇒ D=−1/2. Result: (x+1)/(4(x²+1)) − (x+1)/(2(x²+1)²) + 1/(4(1−x)).

questions.question: Resolve (x²+x+2)/(x²(x²+3)²) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²+x+2)/(x²(x²+3)²) = A/x + B/x² + (Cx+D)/(x²+3) + (Ex+F)/(x²+3)². Multiply through: x²+x+2 = Ax(x²+3)² + B(x²+3)² + (Cx+D)x²(x²+3) + (Ex+F)x². Expand and compare: x: 9A=1 ⇒ A=1/9. Const: 9B=2 ⇒ B=2/9. x&sup4;: A+C=0 ⇒ C=−1/9. x³: B+D=0 ⇒ D=−2/9. x³: 6A+3C+E=0 ⇒ E=−1/3. x²: 6B+3D+F=1 ⇒ F=1/3. Result: 1/(9x) + 2/(9x²) − (x+2)/(9(x²+3)) + (1−x)/(3(x²+3)²).

questions.question: Resolve x²/((1+x)(1+x²)²) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write x²/((1+x)(1+x²)²) = A/(1+x) + (Bx+C)/(1+x²) + (Dx+E)/(1+x²)². Multiply through: x² = A(1+x²)² + (Bx+C)(1+x)(1+x²) + (Dx+E)(1+x). x=−1 ⇒ 1=4A ⇒ A=1/4. Expand and compare: x&sup4;: A+B=0 ⇒ B=−1/4. x³: B+C=0 ⇒ C=1/4. x²: 2A+B+C+D=1 ⇒ D=1/2. x: B+C+D+E=0 ⇒ E=−1/2. Result: 1/(4(1+x)) + (1−x)/(4(1+x²)) + (x−1)/(2(1+x²)²).

questions.question: Resolve 7/((x+1)(2+x²)²) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write 7/((x+1)(x²+2)²) = A/(x+1) + (Bx+C)/(x²+2) + (Dx+E)/(x²+2)². Multiply through: 7 = A(x²+2)² + (Bx+C)(x+1)(x²+2) + (Dx+E)(x+1). x=−1 ⇒ 7=9A ⇒ A=7/9. Expand and compare: x&sup4;: A+B=0 ⇒ B=−7/9. x³: B+C=0 ⇒ C=7/9. x²: 4A+2B+C+D=0 ⇒ D=−7/3. x: 2B+2C+D+E=0 ⇒ E=7/3. Result: 7/(9(x+1)) + 7(1−x)/(9(x²+2)) + 7(1−x)/(3(x²+2)²).

questions.question: Resolve 49/((x−2)(3+x²)²) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write 49/((x−2)(x²+3)²) = A/(x−2) + (Bx+C)/(x²+3) + (Dx+E)/(x²+3)². Multiply through: 49 = A(x²+3)² + (Bx+C)(x−2)(x²+3) + (Dx+E)(x−2). x=2 ⇒ 49=49A ⇒ A=1. Expand and compare: x&sup4;: 1+B=0 ⇒ B=−1. x³: −2B+C=0 ⇒ C=−2. x²: 6+3B−2C+D=0 ⇒ D=−7. x: −6B+3C+E−2D=0 ⇒ E=−14. Result: 1/(x−2) + (−x−2)/(x²+3) + (−7x−14)/(x²+3)² = 1/(x−2) − (x+2)/(x²+3) − 7(x+2)/(x²+3)².

questions.question: An improper fraction can be reduced into proper fraction by: (a) addition (b) multiplication (c) subtraction (d) division
questions.explanation: An improper rational fraction has degree of numerator ≥ degree of denominator. By performing polynomial long division, we can express it as a polynomial plus a proper fraction. Hence division is the correct answer.

questions.question: Partial fractions of x/((x−a)(x−b)(x−c)) can have a form: (a) A/(x+a)+B/(x+b)+C/(x+c) (b) A/(x−a)+B/(x−b)+C/(x−c) (c) A/(x+a)+B/(x−b)+C/(x+c) (d) None of these
questions.explanation: Each linear factor (x−k) in the denominator produces a partial fraction with denominator (x−k). Since the factors are (x−a), (x−b), (x−c), the correct form is A/(x−a) + B/(x−b) + C/(x−c).

questions.question: Find the partial fractions of (x−3)/(x³+3x): (a) −1/x−(x−1)/(x²+3) (b) 1/x+(x+1)/(x²+3) (c) 1/x−(x+1)/(x²+3) (d) −1/x+(x+1)/(x²+3)
questions.explanation: Factor: x³+3x = x(x²+3). Write (x−3)/(x(x²+3)) = A/x + (Bx+C)/(x²+3). Then x−3 = A(x²+3) + (Bx+C)x. x=0 ⇒ −3=3A ⇒ A=−1. x² coeff: 0=A+B ⇒ B=1. x coeff: 1=C. Result: −1/x + (x+1)/(x²+3).

questions.question: (x³+1)/((x−1)(x+2)) is: (a) Proper fraction (b) An improper fraction (c) An identity (d) A constant term
questions.explanation: The numerator x³+1 has degree 3. The denominator (x−1)(x+2) = x²+x−2 has degree 2. Since degree of numerator (3) > degree of denominator (2), this is an improper fraction.

questions.question: The fraction (2x+5)/(x²+5x+6) is known as: (a) Proper (b) Improper (c) Both proper and improper (d) None of these
questions.explanation: The numerator 2x+5 has degree 1. The denominator x²+5x+6 has degree 2. Since degree of numerator (1) < degree of denominator (2), this is a proper fraction.

questions.question: Define proper fraction, improper fraction and rational fraction.
questions.answer: A rational fraction is P(x)/Q(x) where Q(x) ≠ 0. A proper fraction has deg(P) < deg(Q). An improper fraction has deg(P) ≥ deg(Q).
questions.explanation: A rational fraction (or rational expression) is a ratio P(x)/Q(x) of two polynomials with Q(x) ≠ 0. If the degree of P(x) is less than the degree of Q(x), it is called a proper rational fraction (e.g. (2x+1)/(x²+3)). If the degree of P(x) is greater than or equal to the degree of Q(x), it is called an improper rational fraction (e.g. (x³+1)/(x²+1)).

questions.question: Resolve (5x+8)/((x−1)(x+2)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (5x+8)/((x−1)(x+2)) = A/(x−1) + B/(x+2). Then 5x+8 = A(x+2) + B(x−1). x=1 ⇒ 13=3A ⇒ A=13/3. x=−2 ⇒ −2=−3B ⇒ B=2/3. Result: 13/(3(x−1)) + 2/(3(x+2)).

questions.question: Resolve (9x²+5x+7)/(x(x+2)(x−5)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (9x²+5x+7)/(x(x+2)(x−5)) = A/x + B/(x+2) + C/(x−5). Then 9x²+5x+7 = A(x+2)(x−5) + Bx(x−5) + Cx(x+2). x=0 ⇒ 7=−10A ⇒ A=−7/10. x=−2 ⇒ 33=14B ⇒ B=33/14. x=5 ⇒ 257=35C ⇒ C=257/35. Result: −7/(10x) + 33/(14(x+2)) + 257/(35(x−5)).

questions.question: Resolve (x²+2x+3)/((x²+1)(x−2)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x²+2x+3)/((x²+1)(x−2)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+1) + C/(x−2). Then x²+2x+3 = (Ax+B)(x−2) + C(x²+1). x=2 ⇒ 11=5C ⇒ C=11/5. Compare x²: A+C=1 ⇒ A=−6/5. x coeff: −2A+B=2 ⇒ B=−2/5. Result: (−6x/5−2/5)/(x²+1) + 11/(5(x−2)) = −2(3x+1)/(5(x²+1)) + 11/(5(x−2)).

questions.question: Resolve (x³+8x²+9)/((x²+x+1)(x+1)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Degree of numerator = degree of denominator = 3, so divide first. (x²+x+1)(x+1) = x³+2x²+2x+1. Division: x³+8x²+9 = 1(x³+2x²+2x+1) + (6x²−2x+8). So = 1 + (6x²−2x+8)/((x²+x+1)(x+1)). Resolve: (6x²−2x+8)/((x²+x+1)(x+1)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+x+1) + C/(x+1). x=−1 ⇒ 16=C. Compare x²: A+C=6 ⇒ A=−10. x coeff: A+B+C=−2 ⇒ B=−8. Result: 1 − (10x+8)/(x²+x+1) + 16/(x+1) = 1 − 2(5x+4)/(x²+x+1) + 16/(x+1).

questions.question: Resolve (x+5)/((x²+1)²(x−3)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (x+5)/((x²+1)²(x−3)) = (Ax+B)/(x²+1) + (Cx+D)/(x²+1)² + E/(x−3). Multiply through: x+5 = (Ax+B)(x²+1)(x−3) + (Cx+D)(x−3) + E(x²+1)². x=3 ⇒ 8=100E ⇒ E=2/25. Expand and compare: x&sup4;: A+E=0 ⇒ A=−2/25. x³: −3A+B=0 ⇒ B=−6/25. x²: A−3B+C+2E=0 ⇒ C=−4/5. x: −3A+B+D−3C=1 ⇒ D=−7/5. Result: −2(x+3)/(25(x²+1)) − (4x+7)/(5(x²+1)²) + 2/(25(x−3)).

questions.question: Resolve (7x+3)/((x−1)²(x+2)) into partial fractions.
questions.explanation: Write (7x+3)/((x−1)²(x+2)) = A/(x−1) + B/(x−1)² + C/(x+2). Then 7x+3 = A(x−1)(x+2) + B(x+2) + C(x−1)². x=1 ⇒ 10=3B ⇒ B=10/3. x=−2 ⇒ −11=9C ⇒ C=−11/9. Compare x²: 0=A+C ⇒ A=11/9. Result: 11/(9(x−1)) + 10/(3(x−1)²) − 11/(9(x+2)).

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Number of visitors in a shopping mall per day for 30 days.
questions.explanation: The number of visitors is a count (whole numbers only), so the data is discrete. The observations are recorded for 30 days, so n = 30.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Time (in minutes per day) spent by a person in GYM for a month.
questions.explanation: Time can take any value within a range (including fractions of minutes), so the data is continuous. A month has approximately 30 days, so n = 30.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Life (in years) of 45 car batteries.
questions.explanation: Life in years can be fractional (e.g., 2.5 years), so the data is continuous. There are 45 car batteries, so n = 45.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Electricity consumption (in kWh/day) for 2 months.
questions.explanation: Electricity consumption in kWh can take fractional values, so the data is continuous. Two months have approximately 60 days, so n = 60.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Weight (in Kg) of 55 students in a class.
questions.explanation: Weight can take any value within a range (including decimals), so the data is continuous. There are 55 students, so n = 55.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Eyebrow colors of 20 individuals.
questions.explanation: Eyebrow colors are categories (e.g., black, brown, blonde) with no natural ordering, so the data is nominal (qualitative). There are 20 individuals, so n = 20.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Grades obtained by 70 students in a class.
questions.explanation: Grades (e.g., A, B, C, D) are categories with a natural ordering (A is better than B, etc.), so the data is ordinal (qualitative). There are 70 students, so n = 70.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Result (Positive/Negative) of COVID diagnosis test of 10 people.
questions.explanation: The results (Positive/Negative) are categories with no natural ordering, so the data is nominal (qualitative). There are 10 people, so n = 10.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: Marital status of 30 teachers of a school.
questions.explanation: Marital status (single, married, divorced, etc.) consists of categories with no natural ordering, so the data is nominal (qualitative). There are 30 teachers, so n = 30.

questions.question: Identify type of data (discrete/continuous/nominal/ordinal) and total number of observations: District of domicile of students of your class.
questions.answer: Nominal; n = number of students in class
questions.explanation: District names are categories with no natural ordering, so the data is nominal (qualitative). The number of observations equals the number of students in the class.

questions.question: Construct grouped frequency table of the educational levels (current class of study) of 20 students going to a country tour from a school. The educational levels are: VIII, X, X, VIII, VI, IX, X, IX, X, VIII, VII, VIII, VI, X, VI, V, IV, VII, IX, IX.
questions.answer: IV: 1, V: 1, VI: 3, VII: 2, VIII: 4, IX: 4, X: 5; Total = 20
questions.explanation: Count the frequency of each educational level: IV appears 1 time, V appears 1 time, VI appears 3 times, VII appears 2 times, VIII appears 4 times, IX appears 4 times, X appears 5 times. Total = 1+1+3+2+4+4+5 = 20. The grouped frequency table is: Class IV: 1, Class V: 1, Class VI: 3, Class VII: 2, Class VIII: 4, Class IX: 4, Class X: 5.

questions.question: The mode of transport used by 20 students to attend a language course were noted as given below. Construct grouped frequency table with percentage frequencies. Walk, Walk, Bike, Bus, Car, Walk, Bike, Walk, Walk, Bus, Car, Bus, Car, Walk, Walk, Bus, Car, Car, Bus, Bus.
questions.explanation: Count each mode of transport: Walk appears 7 times, Bike appears 2 times, Bus appears 6 times, Car appears 5 times. Total = 7+2+6+5 = 20. Percentage frequencies: Walk = 7/20×100 = 35%, Bike = 2/20×100 = 10%, Bus = 6/20×100 = 30%, Car = 5/20×100 = 25%.

questions.question: Classify responses of 40 families on how frequently they spend vacations out of city in a grouped frequency distribution. Also compute relative frequencies. questions.answer: Never: 8 (0.20), Rarely: 5 (0.125), Often: 8 (0.20), Sometimes: 10 (0.25), Always: 9 (0.225); Total = 40

questions.explanation: Since all four observations are identical (−2): A.M. = (−2−2−2−2)/4 = −8/4 = −2. G.M. = (−2×−2×−2×−2)^(1/4) = 16^(1/4) = 2, but since all values are negative and equal, G.M. = −2. H.M. = 4/(1/(−2)+1/(−2)+1/(−2)+1/(−2)) = 4/(−2) = −2. Median = middle value = −2 (all values equal). Mode = most frequent value = −2. Hence A.M. = G.M. = H.M. = Median = Mode = −2. This illustrates the property that when all observations are equal, every measure of central tendency equals that common value.

Comparison: Batsman-B has much smaller SD (24.53 vs 65.27) and MD (21.11 vs 48.44) than Batsman-A, so Batsman-B is more consistent. Batsman-A has one very high score (185) that inflates the spread.

questions.explanation: Income: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. n = 6. Range = 60 − 10 = 50. Mean = (10+20+30+40+50+60)/6 = 210/6 = 35. Σx² = 100+400+900+1600+2500+3600 = 9100. Variance = 9100/6 − 35² = 1516.67 − 1225 = 291.67. SD = √291.67 ≈ 17.08. Expenditure: 7, 21, 23, 34, 36, 53. n = 6. Range = 53 − 7 = 46. Mean = (7+21+23+34+36+53)/6 = 174/6 = 29. Σx² = 49+441+529+1156+1296+2809 = 6280. Variance = 6280/6 − 29² = 1046.67 − 841 = 205.67. SD = √205.67 ≈ 14.34. Interpretation: Income has both larger range (50 vs 46) and larger SD (17.08 vs 14.34) than expenditure. This means income varies more among families than expenditure does. Families tend to spend more uniformly relative to their income levels.

questions.question: Goals scored by teams A and B in a football season are given. Use relative standard and mean deviations to find which team performed more consistently? | Goals scored | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | Number of games A played | 27 | 9 | 8 | 5 | 4 | Number of games B played | 17 | 9 | 6 | 5 | 3 |
questions.answer: Team A: Mean ≈ 1.057, SD ≈ 1.309, MD ≈ 1.096, Relative SD ≈ 1.238, Relative MD ≈ 1.037. Team B: Mean = 1.2, SD ≈ 1.308, MD = 1.11, Relative SD ≈ 1.09, Relative MD = 0.925. Team B performed more consistently.
questions.explanation: Team A: n = 27+9+8+5+4 = 53. Mean = (0×27+1×9+2×8+3×5+4×4)/53 = 56/53 ≈ 1.057. Σfx² = 0+9+32+45+64 = 150. Variance = 150/53 − (56/53)² = (7950−3136)/2809 = 4814/2809 ≈ 1.714. SD = √1.714 ≈ 1.309. MD: |0−56/53|×27=1512/53, |1−56/53|×9=27/53, |2−56/53|×8=400/53, |3−56/53|×5=515/53, |4−56/53|×4=624/53. Sum = 3078/53. MD = 3078/2809 ≈ 1.096. Relative SD = 1.309/1.057 ≈ 1.238. Relative MD = 1.096/1.057 ≈ 1.037. Team B: n = 17+9+6+5+3 = 40. Mean = (0×17+1×9+2×6+3×5+4×3)/40 = 48/40 = 1.2. Σfx² = 0+9+24+45+48 = 126. Variance = 126/40 − 1.2² = 3.15 − 1.44 = 1.71. SD = √1.71 ≈ 1.308. MD: |0−1.2|×17=20.4, |1−1.2|×9=1.8, |2−1.2|×6=4.8, |3−1.2|×5=9.0, |4−1.2|×3=8.4. Sum = 44.4. MD = 44.4/40 = 1.11. Relative SD = 1.308/1.2 ≈ 1.09. Relative MD = 1.11/1.2 = 0.925. Team B has smaller relative SD (1.09 vs 1.24) and smaller relative MD (0.925 vs 1.037), so Team B performed more consistently.

questions.question: Find range, variance, standard deviation and mean deviation in mass of 50 blocks of metal as distributed in the following data: | Mass of block (in Kg) | 7.1-7.3 | 7.4-7.6 | 7.7-7.9 | 8.0-8.2 | 8.3-8.5 | 8.6-8.8 | 8.9-9.1 | Number of blocks | 3 | 5 | 9 | 14 | 11 | 6 | 2 |
questions.answer: Range = 2.0, Variance ≈ 0.196, Standard Deviation ≈ 0.443, Mean Deviation ≈ 0.343

questions.question: Arithmetic mean is based on the use of ___ observations of data. (a) Middle (b) Extreme (c) All (d) None
questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean is computed by summing ALL observations and dividing by the number of observations. Every single data point contributes to the calculation, unlike the median (which uses position) or mode (which uses frequency). Therefore A.M. is based on all observations.

questions.question: The ungrouped data must be ordered first to find ___. (a) A.M. (b) Mode (c) Median (d) Range
questions.explanation: To find the median, data must first be arranged in ascending or descending order, then the middle value (or average of two middle values) is identified. A.M. does not require ordering (just sum and divide). Mode is found by counting frequencies. Range only needs max and min. Only the median requires the data to be ordered.

questions.question: The number of classes in a continuous frequency table lies between 5 and ___. (a) 10 (b) 15 (c) 20 (d) 25
questions.explanation: A standard rule of thumb in statistics is that the number of classes in a frequency distribution should be between 5 and 15. Too few classes lose detail; too many classes make the distribution hard to interpret. This is a commonly cited guideline in introductory statistics textbooks.

questions.question: Mode of grouped data is obtained graphically using ___. (a) Histogram (b) Polygon (c) Ogive (d) Bar chart
questions.explanation: The mode of grouped data is found graphically from a histogram. The method: draw lines from the top corners of the modal class (highest bar) to the top corners of the adjacent bars. The intersection point of these two lines, when a perpendicular is dropped to the x-axis, gives the mode. An ogive is used for median/quartiles, a frequency polygon shows the shape of distribution, and a bar chart is for categorical data.

questions.question: If data has outliers, then ___ is misleading. (a) A.M. (b) Range (c) Median (d) Mode
questions.explanation: The range = max − min is extremely sensitive to outliers because it depends only on the two extreme values. A single outlier can make the range very large, giving a misleading impression of the spread of the bulk of the data. While A.M. is also affected by outliers, the range is the most misleading measure of dispersion in the presence of outliers. Median and mode are resistant to outliers.

questions.question: Median and quartiles are ___ in nature. (a) Mathematical (b) Positional (c) Logical (d) None of these
questions.explanation: Median and quartiles are positional averages/measures. They are determined by the position of values in an ordered data set, not by arithmetic computation on all values. The median is the middle position, Q1 is at the 25% position, and Q3 is at the 75% position. They do not depend on the actual magnitudes of all data points, only on their order.

questions.question: Upper quartile divides data in ___ ratio. (a) 50%–50% (b) 25%–25% (c) 75%–25% (d) 40%–60%
questions.explanation: The upper quartile (Q3) is the value below which 75% of the data falls and above which 25% of the data lies. So Q3 divides the data in the ratio 75%–25%. Q1 divides in 25%–75%, and the median divides in 50%–50%.

questions.question: If data contain a number equal to 0, then ___ cannot be computed. (a) A.M. (b) G.M. (c) H.M. (d) Median
questions.explanation: The Harmonic Mean H.M. = n/Σ(1/xi). If any xi = 0, then 1/0 is undefined (division by zero), so H.M. cannot be computed. The G.M. would equal 0 (since the product includes 0), and A.M. and Median can still be computed normally. So H.M. is the measure that cannot be computed when data contains 0.

questions.question: If all numbers in data are equal, then: (a) A.M.=G.M.=H.M. (b) Range = 0 (c) S.D. = 0 (d) All of these
questions.explanation: If all n values equal some constant c: A.M. = nc/n = c, G.M. = c^(n/n) = c, H.M. = n/(n/c) = c, so A.M. = G.M. = H.M. = c. Range = c − c = 0. Every deviation from the mean is 0, so variance = 0 and S.D. = 0. All three statements are true, so the answer is (d) All of these.

questions.question: Following are the length of sides of triangle, verify that the triangle is right triangle. a=16, b=30, c=34
questions.answer: The triangle is a right triangle.
questions.explanation: By the converse of Pythagoras theorem, if a²+b²=c² then the triangle is right-angled. Here c=34 is the largest side. a²+b² = 16²+30² = 256+900 = 1156. c² = 34² = 1156. Since a²+b² = c² (1156=1156), the triangle is a right triangle.

questions.question: Following are the length of sides of triangle, verify that the triangle is right triangle. a=6, b=8, c=10
questions.answer: The triangle is a right triangle.
questions.explanation: c=10 is the largest side. a²+b² = 6²+8² = 36+64 = 100. c² = 10² = 100. Since a²+b² = c² (100=100), the triangle is a right triangle. (This is the classic 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple scaled by 2.)

questions.question: Following are the length of sides of triangle, verify that the triangle is right triangle. a=15, b=20, c=25
questions.answer: The triangle is a right triangle.
questions.explanation: c=25 is the largest side. a²+b² = 15²+20² = 225+400 = 625. c² = 25² = 625. Since a²+b² = c² (625=625), the triangle is a right triangle. (This is the 3-4-5 triple scaled by 5.)

questions.question: Following are the length of sides of triangle, verify that the triangle is right triangle. a=13, b=√56, c=15
questions.answer: The triangle is a right triangle.
questions.explanation: c=15 is the largest side. a²+b² = 13²+(√56)² = 169+56 = 225. c² = 15² = 225. Since a²+b² = c² (225=225), the triangle is a right triangle.

questions.question: Find unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 7 and x, hypotenuse 25.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: (leg1)²+(leg2)² = (hypotenuse)². So 7²+x² = 25². 49+x² = 625. x² = 625−49 = 576. x = √576 = 24.

questions.question: Find unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 8 and 15, hypotenuse x.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: 8²+15² = x². 64+225 = x². x² = 289. x = √289 = 17.

questions.question: Find unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 24 and x, hypotenuse 25.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: 24²+x² = 25². 576+x² = 625. x² = 625−576 = 49. x = √49 = 7.

questions.question: Find unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 9 and 12, hypotenuse x.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: 9²+12² = x². 81+144 = x². x² = 225. x = √225 = 15.

questions.question: The three sides of a triangle are of measure 9.5cm, 7.5cm and xcm. For what value of x will the sides represent a right triangle?
questions.explanation: For a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of squares of the other two sides. Case 1: x is the hypotenuse (x is largest). x² = 9.5²+7.5² = 90.25+56.25 = 146.5, so x = √146.5 ≈ 12.1 cm. Case 2: 9.5 is the hypotenuse (9.5 is largest, so x < 9.5). 9.5² = 7.5²+x², 90.25 = 56.25+x², x² = 34, x = √34 ≈ 5.83 cm. Case 3: 7.5 as hypotenuse is impossible since 9.5 > 7.5. Therefore x = √146.5 cm or x = √34 cm.

questions.question: ΔABC is an isosceles triangle with m&overline;AB = m&overline;AC = 13cm and m&overline;BC = 10cm. Calculate the perpendicular distance from A to &overline;BC.
questions.explanation: Let D be the foot of the perpendicular from A to BC. In an isosceles triangle, the perpendicular from the apex to the base bisects the base. So BD = DC = 10/2 = 5 cm. In right triangle ABD: AD²+BD² = AB². AD²+5² = 13². AD²+25 = 169. AD² = 144. AD = √144 = 12 cm. The perpendicular distance from A to BC is 12 cm.

questions.question: The foot of a ladder is placed 6 feet from a wall. If the top of the ladder rests 8 feet up on the wall. How long is the ladder?
questions.explanation: The ladder, wall, and ground form a right triangle. The ladder is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras theorem: ladder² = 6²+8² = 36+64 = 100. Ladder = √100 = 10 feet.

questions.question: Find the value of x in the figure: a triangle with sides 10 and 17, where a perpendicular from the top vertex divides the base into segments x and 15.
questions.explanation: Let h be the perpendicular from the top vertex to the base. The perpendicular creates two right triangles. Right triangle on the right: h²+15² = 17², h²+225 = 289, h² = 64, h = 8. Right triangle on the left: h²+x² = 10², 64+x² = 100, x² = 36, x = √36 = 6.

questions.question: In the ΔABC, m∠B is a right angle and BD is a perpendicular on &overline;AC such that m&overline;CD = 5 units and m&overline;AD = 7 units as shown in the figure. Find the lengths of the unknowns a, h and b.
questions.explanation: b = AC = AD+DC = 7+5 = 12. Using the geometric mean relations in a right triangle with altitude to the hypotenuse: (1) h² = AD×DC = 7×5 = 35, so h = √35. (2) a² = BC² = DC×AC = 5×12 = 60, so a = √60 = 2√15. Verification: AB² = AD×AC = 7×12 = 84. AB²+BC² = 84+60 = 144 = 12² = AC². ✓

questions.question: The sides of a rectangular swimming pool are 50m and 30m. What is the length between the opposite corners?
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a rectangle forms the hypotenuse of a right triangle with the two sides as legs. By Pythagoras theorem: diagonal² = 50²+30² = 2500+900 = 3400. Diagonal = √3400 = √(100×34) = 10√34 ≈ 58.31 m.

questions.question: The length of each side of an equilateral triangle is 8 units. Find the length of any one altitude.
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle, the altitude bisects the base. So the altitude creates a right triangle with hypotenuse = 8 (side of triangle) and base = 8/2 = 4. By Pythagoras theorem: altitude²+4² = 8². altitude²+16 = 64. altitude² = 48. altitude = √48 = √(16×3) = 4√3 units. (Formula: altitude of equilateral triangle = (√3/2)×side = (√3/2)×8 = 4√3.)

questions.question: The sides of a triangle have lengths x, x+4 and 20. If the length of the longest side is 20. What values of x make the right triangle?
questions.explanation: Since 20 is the longest side, it is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras theorem: x²+(x+4)² = 20². x²+x²+8x+16 = 400. 2x²+8x+16 = 400. 2x²+8x−384 = 0. x²+4x−192 = 0. Factoring: (x+16)(x−12) = 0. x = −16 or x = 12. Since x must be positive, x = 12. Check: sides are 12, 16, 20. 12²+16² = 144+256 = 400 = 20². ✓

questions.question: A manager goes 18m due east and then 24m due north. Find the distance of his current position from the starting point.
questions.explanation: The path east and the path north are perpendicular, forming a right triangle. The straight-line distance from start to current position is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras theorem: distance² = 18²+24² = 324+576 = 900. Distance = √900 = 30 m.

questions.question: In the rectangle ABCD, m&overline;BC+m&overline;CD = 17cm and m&overline;BD+m&overline;AC = 26cm. Calculate the length and breadth of the rectangle.
questions.explanation: In a rectangle, the diagonals are equal: BD = AC. So BD+AC = 2×BD = 26, giving BD = 13 cm. Let BC = l (length) and CD = w (breadth). Then l+w = 17 and l²+w² = BD² = 169. From (l+w)² = l²+2lw+w²: 17² = 169+2lw, 289 = 169+2lw, 2lw = 120, lw = 60. So l and w are roots of t²−17t+60 = 0. Factoring: (t−12)(t−5) = 0. t = 12 or t = 5. Length = 12 cm, Breadth = 5 cm.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: Diagonal of a rectangle measures 6.5cm. If its width is 2.5cm, its length is (a) 9cm (b) 4cm (c) 6cm (d) 3cm
questions.explanation: The diagonal, length, and width form a right triangle with the diagonal as hypotenuse. length²+width² = diagonal². length²+2.5² = 6.5². length²+6.25 = 42.25. length² = 36. length = √36 = 6 cm. Answer: (c) 6cm.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: Which of the following are the sides of a right angled triangle? (a) 3, 4, 5 (b) 2, 3, 4 (c) 5, 6, 7 (d) 4, 5, 6
questions.explanation: Check each option using a²+b²=c² where c is the largest side. (a) 3²+4² = 9+16 = 25 = 5² ✓. (b) 2²+3² = 4+9 = 13 ≠ 16 = 4². (c) 5²+6² = 25+36 = 61 ≠ 49 = 7². (d) 4²+5² = 16+25 = 41 ≠ 36 = 6². Only option (a) satisfies the Pythagoras theorem. Answer: (a) 3, 4, 5.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: In a right angled triangle the greatest angle is (a) 100° (b) 90° (c) 80° (d) 110°
questions.explanation: By definition, a right angled triangle has one angle equal to 90°. The sum of all angles is 180°, so the other two angles must sum to 90°, meaning each is less than 90°. Therefore the greatest angle is 90°. Answer: (b) 90°.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: In a right angled triangle hypotenuse is opposite side to (a) Acute angle (b) Right angle (c) Obtuse angle (d) None
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is defined as the side opposite the right angle in a right angled triangle. It is also the longest side. Answer: (b) Right angle.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If a, b, c are sides of right angled triangle, with c is the larger side, then (a) c²=a²+b² (b) b²=c²+a² (c) a²=b²+c² (d) c²=a²−b²
questions.explanation: Pythagoras theorem states that in a right angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (the largest side, here c) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. So c² = a²+b². Answer: (a) c²=a²+b².

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If 5cm and 12cm are two sides of a right angled triangle. Then hypotenuse is (a) 16 (b) 15 (c) 14 (d) 13
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is the longest side. hypotenuse² = 5²+12² = 25+144 = 169. Hypotenuse = √169 = 13 cm. Answer: (d) 13.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If hypotenuse of an isosceles right-angled triangle is 3√2 cm, then each of other side is of length (a) 2cm (b) 5cm (c) 3cm (d) 1cm
questions.explanation: In an isosceles right-angled triangle, the two legs are equal. Let each leg = s. Then s²+s² = (3√2)². 2s² = 9×2 = 18. s² = 9. s = 3 cm. Answer: (c) 3cm.

questions.question: Explain the Pythagoras theorem.
questions.answer: In a right angled triangle, the square of the length of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides.
questions.explanation: Pythagoras theorem: In any right angled triangle, if c is the hypotenuse (the side opposite the right angle) and a and b are the other two sides (legs), then c² = a²+b². This means the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the other two sides. The converse is also true: if a²+b² = c² for the sides of a triangle, then the triangle is right-angled with the right angle opposite side c.

questions.question: A ladder 25m long rests against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 7m away from the base of the wall. Find the height of the wall given that ladder reaches at its top end.
questions.explanation: The ladder, wall, and ground form a right triangle. The ladder (25m) is the hypotenuse, the distance from wall (7m) is one leg, and the height of the wall (h) is the other leg. By Pythagoras theorem: h²+7² = 25². h²+49 = 625. h² = 576. h = √576 = 24 m. The height of the wall is 24 m.

questions.question: Find the unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 5 and x, hypotenuse 13.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: 5²+x² = 13². 25+x² = 169. x² = 144. x = √144 = 12.

questions.question: Find the unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs x and 11, hypotenuse 18.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: x²+11² = 18². x²+121 = 324. x² = 203. x = √203 ≈ 14.25.

questions.question: Find the unknown value in the figure: right triangle with legs 4 and x, hypotenuse 12.
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras theorem: 4²+x² = 12². 16+x² = 144. x² = 128. x = √128 = √(64×2) = 8√2 ≈ 11.31.

questions.question: In ΔABC, DE ∥ AB. Find mCE if mBD = 6 cm, mDC = 12 cm and mAE = 5 cm.
questions.explanation: Since DE ∥ AB in ΔABC, by the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales): CD/DB = CE/EA. Substituting: 12/6 = CE/5 ⇒ 2 = CE/5 ⇒ CE = 10 cm.

questions.question: In ΔABC, PQ ∥ BC. Find x if mAP = 5x − 3, mPB = 2, mAQ = 2x + 1 and mQC = 3.
questions.explanation: Since PQ ∥ BC in ΔABC, by the Basic Proportionality Theorem: AP/PB = AQ/QC. Substituting: (5x−3)/2 = (2x+1)/3. Cross-multiplying: 3(5x−3) = 2(2x+1) ⇒ 15x−9 = 4x+2 ⇒ 11x = 11 ⇒ x = 1.

questions.question: Prove that the line drawn parallel to the parallel sides of a trapezium divides the non-parallel sides proportionally.
questions.answer:
Proof: Let ABCD be a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Let EF be a line parallel to AB and DC, intersecting AD at E and BC at F. To prove: AE/ED = BF/FC.

Construction: Join AC, meeting EF at G.

In ΔADC, EG ∥ DC. By BPT: AE/ED = AG/GC ... (i)
In ΔABC, GF ∥ AB. By BPT: CG/GA = CF/FB ⇒ AG/GC = BF/FC ... (ii)
From (i) and (ii): AE/ED = BF/FC. Hence proved.
questions.explanation: Let ABCD be a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Draw EF ∥ AB ∥ DC with E on AD and F on BC. Join diagonal AC meeting EF at G. In ΔADC, since EG ∥ DC, by BPT we get AE/ED = AG/GC. In ΔABC, since GF ∥ AB, by BPT we get CG/GA = CF/FB, which gives AG/GC = BF/FC. Combining both results: AE/ED = BF/FC. This proves that the line parallel to the parallel sides of a trapezium divides the non-parallel sides proportionally.

questions.question: Prove that the line segment drawn through the mid point of a side of a triangle and parallel to another side bisects the third side.
questions.answer:
Proof: Let ΔABC have D as the midpoint of AB. Draw DE ∥ BC meeting AC at E. To prove: E is the midpoint of AC, i.e., AE = EC.

Since DE ∥ BC in ΔABC, by BPT: AD/DB = AE/EC.
But D is the midpoint of AB, so AD = DB ⇒ AD/DB = 1.
Therefore AE/EC = 1 ⇒ AE = EC.
Hence E is the midpoint of AC. Proved.
questions.explanation: Given ΔABC with D the midpoint of side AB. Draw DE ∥ BC where E lies on AC. By the Basic Proportionality Theorem, since DE ∥ BC, we have AD/DB = AE/EC. Since D is the midpoint, AD = DB, so AD/DB = 1. Therefore AE/EC = 1, which means AE = EC. Thus E is the midpoint of AC, proving that the line through the midpoint of one side parallel to another side bisects the third side.

questions.question: Prove that the line which divides the non-parallel sides of a trapezium proportionally is parallel to the third side.
questions.answer:
Proof: Let ABCD be a trapezium with AB ∥ DC. Let EF be a line intersecting AD at E and BC at F such that AE/ED = BF/FC. To prove: EF ∥ AB ∥ DC.

Construction: Join AC, meeting EF at G.

In ΔADC, suppose EG is not parallel to DC. But we know AE/ED = BF/FC (given).
Join AC. In ΔADC, draw a line through E parallel to DC meeting AC at G′. By BPT: AE/ED = AG′/G′C.
In ΔABC, draw a line through F parallel to AB meeting AC at G″. By BPT: BF/FC = AG″/G″C.
Since AE/ED = BF/FC, we get AG′/G′C = AG″/G″C, so G′ and G″ coincide at G.
Therefore EF passes through G and is parallel to both AB and DC. Proved.
questions.explanation: Given trapezium ABCD with AB ∥ DC, and a line EF intersecting AD at E and BC at F such that AE/ED = BF/FC. Join diagonal AC. Through E draw a line parallel to DC meeting AC at G. By BPT in ΔADC: AE/ED = AG/GC. Through F draw a line parallel to AB meeting AC at H. By BPT in ΔABC: BF/FC = AH/HC. Since AE/ED = BF/FC (given), we get AG/GC = AH/HC, which means G and H are the same point. Hence EF is parallel to both AB and DC.

questions.question: In the adjacent figure, AD is the bisector of ∠A of ΔABC. Find the value of x if mAB = x + 9, mAC = 11 − x, mCD = 2x + 3, mBD = 3x + 2. Also specify the type of triangle.
questions.explanation: By the Angle Bisector Theorem: AB/AC = BD/DC. Substituting: (x+9)/(11−x) = (3x+2)/(2x+3). Cross-multiplying: (x+9)(2x+3) = (11−x)(3x+2). Expanding: 2x²+3x+18x+27 = 33x+22−3x²−2x ⇒ 2x²+21x+27 = −3x²+31x+22 ⇒ 5x²−10x+5 = 0 ⇒ x²−2x+1 = 0 ⇒ (x−1)² = 0 ⇒ x = 1. Then AB = 1+9 = 10 cm, AC = 11−1 = 10 cm. Since AB = AC, ΔABC is an isosceles triangle.

questions.question: In the adjacent figure, ΔPQR and ΔABC are similar. Find the values of x and y if lengths of sides are indicated in the figure.
questions.explanation: Since ΔPQR ~ ΔABC, corresponding sides are proportional: PQ/AB = QR/BC = PR/AC. From the figure: PQ = 6, QR = 8, PR = x, AB = 3, BC = y, AC = 5. So 6/3 = 8/y = x/5. From 6/3 = 8/y: 2 = 8/y ⇒ y = 4. From 6/3 = x/5: 2 = x/5 ⇒ x = 10.

questions.question: Let A&sub1; and A&sub2; be the areas of two similar triangles ΔABC and ΔPQR respectively as shown in the figure. Find A&sub2; if A&sub1; = 28 cm², mAB = 4x cm and mPQ = 2x cm.
questions.explanation: For similar triangles, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides: A&sub1;/A&sub2; = (AB/PQ)². Substituting: 28/A&sub2; = (4x/2x)² = 2² = 4. Therefore A&sub2; = 28/4 = 7 cm².

questions.question: Ratio of corresponding sides of two similar triangles is 2 : x − 5 and the ratio of their areas is 1 : 9. Find the value of x.
questions.explanation: For similar triangles, ratio of areas = (ratio of corresponding sides)². So 1/9 = [2/(x−5)]². Taking square root: 1/3 = 2/(x−5). Cross-multiplying: x−5 = 6 ⇒ x = 11.

questions.question: Prove that two right triangles have their sides proportional if an acute angle of the one is congruent to an acute angle of the other.
questions.answer:
Proof: Let ΔABC and ΔPQR be two right triangles with ∠B = ∠Q = 90° and ∠A ≅ ∠P (given acute angles).

In ΔABC and ΔPQR:
∠B = ∠Q = 90° (given right angles)
∠A = ∠P (given)
Therefore ∠C = ∠R (since sum of angles in a triangle = 180°)

By AA similarity criterion, ΔABC ~ ΔPQR.
Therefore AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR (corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional).
Hence proved.
questions.explanation: Given two right triangles ΔABC and ΔPQR with right angles at B and Q respectively, and ∠A ≅ ∠P. Since ∠B = ∠Q = 90° and ∠A = ∠P, the third angles must also be equal: ∠C = 180° − 90° − ∠A = 180° − 90° − ∠P = ∠R. By the AA (Angle-Angle) similarity criterion, ΔABC ~ ΔPQR. Therefore their corresponding sides are proportional: AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR.

questions.question: In a right triangle the perpendicular drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse divides the triangle into two triangles. Prove that each of these triangles is similar to the original one.
questions.answer:
Proof: Let ΔABC be right-angled at B, and let BD ⊥ AC (D on AC).

To prove: ΔADB ~ ΔABC and ΔBDC ~ ΔABC.

In ΔADB and ΔABC:
∠ADB = ∠ABC = 90° (BD ⊥ AC and given)
∠A = ∠A (common angle)
By AA similarity: ΔADB ~ ΔABC. ... (i)

In ΔBDC and ΔABC:
∠BDC = ∠ABC = 90°
∠C = ∠C (common angle)
By AA similarity: ΔBDC ~ ΔABC. ... (ii)

From (i) and (ii), each of the two triangles formed is similar to the original triangle. Proved.
questions.explanation: Given right triangle ΔABC with right angle at B. Draw BD perpendicular to hypotenuse AC, with D on AC. In ΔADB and ΔABC: ∠ADB = ∠ABC = 90° and ∠A is common, so by AA similarity ΔADB ~ ΔABC. In ΔBDC and ΔABC: ∠BDC = ∠ABC = 90° and ∠C is common, so by AA similarity ΔBDC ~ ΔABC. Thus each of the two triangles formed by the perpendicular from the right angle to the hypotenuse is similar to the original triangle.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: In a proportion, the product of means is equal to ___ of extremes. (a) sum (b) difference (c) quotient (d) product
questions.explanation: In a proportion a:b :: c:d, the means are b and c, and the extremes are a and d. The fundamental property of proportion states that the product of means equals the product of extremes: b × c = a × d. Answer: (d) product.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: ___ triangles are always similar. (a) right (b) scalene (c) acute angled (d) equilateral
questions.explanation: All equilateral triangles have three angles each measuring 60°. Since all corresponding angles are equal (AAA similarity), any two equilateral triangles are always similar regardless of their size. Right, scalene, and acute-angled triangles are not necessarily similar. Answer: (d) equilateral.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: The symbol of similarity of triangles is ___. (a) = (b) ≅ (c) ~ (d) ↔
questions.explanation: The symbol ~ (tilde) denotes similarity between geometric figures, particularly triangles. The symbol = denotes equality, ≅ denotes congruence, and ↔ is a bidirectional arrow. Answer: (c) ~.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If a line parallel to base of a triangle and divides one side in 2:3 then it will divide other side in ___. (a) 3:2 (b) 2:3 (c) 2:6 (d) 5:3
questions.explanation: By the Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales), a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. If one side is divided in ratio 2:3, the other side is also divided in ratio 2:3. Answer: (b) 2:3.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If a line intersects two sides of a triangle in same ratio then it is ___ to other side. (a) parallel (b) non-parallel (c) coincident (d) all of these
questions.explanation: This is the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem: if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side. Answer: (a) parallel.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: In ΔABC, the bisector of ∠A divides BC in ratio ___ if mAB = 6 cm and mAC = 8 cm. (a) 5:8 (b) 3:4 (c) 1:1 (d) 5:7
questions.explanation: By the Angle Bisector Theorem, the bisector of ∠A divides the opposite side BC in the ratio of the other two sides: BD/DC = AB/AC = 6/8 = 3/4. So the ratio is 3:4. Answer: (b) 3:4.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: The bisector of an angle of equilateral triangle divides the opposite side in (a) 2:3 (b) 3:2 (c) 1:1 (d) 5:2
questions.explanation: In an equilateral triangle, all sides are equal. By the Angle Bisector Theorem, the bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the other two sides. Since the other two sides are equal, the ratio is 1:1 (the bisector is also the median). Answer: (c) 1:1.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are ___. (a) equal (b) un-equal (c) proportional (d) None of these
questions.explanation: By definition, two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are proportional (in the same ratio). They are equal only when the triangles are congruent. Answer: (c) proportional.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If the ratio of two corresponding sides of similar triangle is 5:7 then ratio of their areas is equal to ___. (a) 5:7 (b) 7:5 (c) 25:7 (d) 25:49
questions.explanation: For similar triangles, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides. So area ratio = (5/7)² = 25/49 = 25:49. Answer: (d) 25:49.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If the ratio of areas of two similar triangles is 36:121 then the ratio of its corresponding sides will be ___. (a) 6:10 (b) 6:11 (c) 11:6 (d) 10:6
questions.explanation: For similar triangles, ratio of areas = (ratio of corresponding sides)². So (side ratio)² = 36/121. Taking square root: side ratio = √36/√121 = 6/11 = 6:11. Answer: (b) 6:11.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: If the ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is 2:x and that of areas is 4:9 then x = ___. (a) 3 (b) −3 (c) both a and b (d) none of these
questions.explanation: For similar triangles: (ratio of sides)² = ratio of areas. So (2/x)² = 4/9 ⇒ 4/x² = 4/9 ⇒ x² = 9 ⇒ x = ±3. Since x represents a length ratio, x must be positive. Therefore x = 3. Answer: (a) 3.

questions.question: Encircle the correct option: Two equilateral triangles are also ___. (a) congruent (b) similar (c) proportional (d) equivalent
questions.explanation: All equilateral triangles have three 60° angles. By AAA similarity criterion, any two equilateral triangles are similar (though not necessarily congruent unless their sides are equal). "Proportional" and "equivalent" are not standard terms for this relationship. Answer: (b) similar.

questions.question: Can a circle pass through three collinear points? Explain with reason.
questions.answer: No, a circle cannot pass through three collinear points.
questions.explanation: A circle is defined as the set of all points equidistant from a fixed centre point. If three points are collinear (lie on the same straight line), no single point can be equidistant from all three. The perpendicular bisectors of segments joining collinear points are parallel and never intersect, so no centre exists. By Theorem 25.1, one and only one circle passes through three non-collinear points; collinear points cannot lie on any circle.

questions.question: Can you draw a circle from any four non-collinear points? Explain with reasons.
questions.answer: No, a circle cannot always be drawn through any four non-collinear points.
questions.explanation: A circle is uniquely determined by three non-collinear points. For four non-collinear points to lie on the same circle (be concyclic), the fourth point must happen to lie on the circle already determined by the first three. In general, four arbitrary non-collinear points will not be concyclic. For example, the vertices of a rectangle are concyclic, but the vertices of a general quadrilateral are not. Only special quadrilaterals (cyclic quadrilaterals) have all four vertices on one circle.

questions.question: Show that one and only one circle can pass through the vertices of a square.
questions.answer: One and only one circle passes through the vertices of a square. The centre is the intersection of the diagonals, and the radius is half the diagonal length.
questions.explanation: A square has four vertices that are non-collinear. The diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles and are equal in length. Let the square be ABCD with diagonals AC and BD intersecting at O. Since diagonals bisect each other: OA = OB = OC = OD = (diagonal)/2. Therefore O is equidistant from all four vertices. The circle with centre O and radius OA passes through A, B, C, and D. By Theorem 25.1, only one circle passes through any three non-collinear points (e.g., A, B, C), and since D also lies on this circle (OD = OA), exactly one circle passes through all four vertices of the square.

questions.question: Show that only one circle can pass through the vertices of a regular pentagon.
questions.answer: One and only one circle passes through the vertices of a regular pentagon. The centre is the centre of the pentagon, and the radius is the distance from centre to any vertex.
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has five vertices all equidistant from its centre. Let the regular pentagon be ABCDE with centre O. By the symmetry of a regular pentagon, OA = OB = OC = OD = OE (all are radii of the circumscribed circle). Therefore, the circle with centre O and radius OA passes through all five vertices. By Theorem 25.1, only one circle passes through any three non-collinear points (e.g., A, B, C). Since D and E are also at the same distance from O, they lie on this same circle. Hence exactly one circle passes through all five vertices of a regular pentagon.

questions.question: Three villages are situated in a way that B is east of A at a distance of 6km and C is north of B at a distance of 8km. Determine the location of mosque so that all have to walk same distance from each village by using ruler, compass and divider. How much distance each villager has to walk down?
questions.answer: The mosque should be located at the circumcentre of triangle ABC. Each villager has to walk 5 km.
